precepts.text: Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: until Israel brought forth. Then the remnant of Christ's brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. Why? Because we fell. Now he's raising us up as in the days of old. We're coming back to who we are.
precepts.point: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Why does it have to be raised up? Because we fell.

Micah shows the order of it: “Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth.” God gave Israel up until the woman in travail, Israel, brought forth. “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” Then the remnant of Christ's brethren returns to the children of Israel.

That is the tabernacle of David being raised. We were given up and we fell, and now he is raising us up as in the days of old. We are coming back to who we are.

precepts.text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel. Article read in class: the unblemished passover lambs were raised at Migdal Eder, the tower of the flock by Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice; the same road Christ walked, born in Bethlehem and offered at Jerusalem during Passover.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The lambs without blemish were raised in Bethlehem and slaughtered in Jerusalem. Same thing as Jesus Christ. So the prophecy: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Christ was born in Bethlehem. An article read in the class shows how our forefathers handled the passover lambs: the high priests given charge over them brought forth lambs without blemish from Migdal Eder in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought them to Jerusalem for sacrifice. Migdal Eder means the tower of the flock, the same tower of the flock read about in Micah the fourth chapter, the eighth verse.

This Jesus was born in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and eventually brought to Jerusalem during passover, where he offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins. The same road as the lambs.

precepts.text: I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.
precepts.point: When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
“And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.”

That is what Joshua did to all those kings, with no favour and none left to breathe, and it shall happen again: vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard, laid upon Edom by the hand of Israel. This is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

precepts.text: They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek; this was fulfilled in Christ, not Solomon.
precepts.point: The Lord promised that His mercy would not depart from him as it did from Saul, and that David's house, kingdom, and throne would be established for ever. The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that He might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
The Lord said of David's seed, “If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men.” Solomon was not chastened with the rod of men in his lifetime.

Micah shows who was: “they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.” That was fulfilled in Christ, not Solomon. Jesus the Christ was smitten with the rod upon the cheek, and he did no sin, though it was Solomon who sinned.

The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that he might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

precepts.text: Out of Bethlehem shall come forth the ruler in Israel, whose goings forth have been from everlasting.
precepts.point: The Lord promised that His mercy would not depart from him as it did from Saul, and that David's house, kingdom, and throne would be established for ever. The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that He might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Out of Bethlehem, the city of David, comes the ruler in Israel. His goings forth have been from everlasting, and that is the one whose throne the Lord said “shall be established for ever.” The same judge of Israel smitten with a rod upon the cheek is the ruler who came forth out of Bethlehem: Jesus Christ, of David's line.

precepts.text: The remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles as a lion among the beasts, treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver, and every enemy shall be cut off; another proof we were scattered everywhere like the dew and rain, and a picture of the strength the Most High returns to us.
precepts.point: He enlarges David's steps under him so his feet do not slip; David pursues his enemies, overtakes them, and does not turn again till they are consumed.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“He teacheth my hands to war”, David says, and “I have pursued mine enemies, and overtaken them: neither did I turn again till they were consumed.” Micah shows the remnant of Jacob with that same strength in the last days.

“And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the Lord, as the showers upon the grass”. That is another proof we were scattered everywhere, like the dew and the rain falling on the whole earth.

Then the strength returns: “the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.” Treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver is David wounding his enemies so they cannot rise, fallen under his feet.

“Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off.” Every enemy cut off: that is the Most High giving us the necks of our enemies, and it is a picture of the strength he returns to us.

precepts.text: The prophecy the priests were quoting: out of Bethlehem Ephratah shall he come forth that is to be ruler in Israel.
precepts.point: The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
Herod “demanded of them where Christ should be born. And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet”. The chief priests and scribes answered at once. They knew the scriptures concerning the messiah.

The prophet they quoted is Micah: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.” Out of Bethlehem Ephratah, little among the thousands of Judah, comes he that is to be ruler in Israel, the Governor “that shall rule my people Israel.” His goings forth are from of old, from everlasting. The priests had the verse; they could name the town before the child was found in it.

When we got to the promised land, ten of the spies said they are giants; Caleb and Joshua said we can overcome them. It is the same again: we have to subdue the earth. “And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people”: that is the planet earth. “As a young lion among the flocks of sheep”: not an old lion, a young lion in his prime. “Who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.”
